messages:
maria: quick heads-up — found two problematic bits in the v1->v2 migration guide: the streaming example still uses the old `response_stream` param (v2 uses `stream` and the chunk format changed) and the embed model-swap note doesn't document fallback routing semantics. this will break our Rust/Go snippets when users try streaming.

kevin: can you paste the exact snippet and a minimal corrected example? i can pick up the PR if its straightforward.

maria: sure. current (broken) JSON example in the guide:
```json
{"model":"text-chat-v1","response_stream":true,"input":"Hello"}
```
Minimal v2-correct example we should use instead:
```json
{"model":"chat-v2","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}
```
Also want a short note in the "Model swaps" section: older embed aliases may be auto-routed to a compatible variant but could return lower-dimension vectors or slower performance. recommend explicitly listing `embed-regular-v2` as an explicit fallback in docs and examples to avoid surprises.

docs-bot: created ticket DOCS-8921: Update migration guide streaming param + embed fallback callout (labels: docs, needs-review). https://git.company.internal/r/redwood/docs/issues/8921 :spiral_note_pad: 

oliver: i'll open a lightweight PR. question: update all language snippets (Rust/Go/TS) across the site or just the canonical migration and streaming pages first?

maria: canonical pages first: guides/migration and api/streaming. after that run a grep/replace for `response_stream` in the repo and handle matches case-by-case. leave examples that intentionally show legacy behavior alone.

sam: should we add a short changelog blurb for the release notes? some customers still call the old param name in automation.

maria: yes — under Breaking Changes add: "streaming parameter renamed from `response_stream` to `stream`. Calls using the old param will be routed, but please migrate to `stream` to avoid future errors." include the embed fallback sentence as well. keep it concise.

kevin: additionally, can we add a docs lint to catch `response_stream` in markdown? i can prototype an MDX linter rule (eslint plugin) to flag it so we catch regressions.

oliver: PR opened: branch docs/param-rename-embed-fallback, title: "docs: replace response_stream with stream + add embed fallback note". includes updated JSON/Rust/TS snippets on migration and streaming pages and a small grep-based test. link: https://git.company.internal/r/redwood/docs/pulls/1245 (WIP)

docs-bot: PR 1245 created, added to docs CI queue. scheduled staging deploy 2026-03-25T03:00Z if CI passes.

maria: perfect — thanks. once CI is green i'll add the release-note blurb to the 2.0.0 changelog draft and ping product for signoff. :tada:
